# PreFlight

> PreFlight sends a swarm of AI agents to test your web app like real users. Every bug they find comes back with evidence and a fix pull request.

## What it does

- A swarm of AI agents explores your web application in real browsers, acting like first-time users instead of following scripts.
- Every finding ships with evidence: screenshots, console logs, and network traces.
- Root-cause diagnosis pairs what the agents observed in the browser with your repository source code.
- When the swarm is confident in a repair, it opens a GitHub pull request with the fix. A human merge gate always applies. Nothing is ever pushed directly to your branches.

## How it works

1. Install the PreFlight QA GitHub App and connect a repository you own.
2. Run a swarm against a deployment of your app.
3. Review findings, each with attached evidence.
4. Merge the fix pull requests you want.

## Who it is for

Developers and teams shipping web applications who want real-user testing without writing and maintaining end-to-end test scripts.

## Access

PreFlight is currently invite-only. Join the waitlist by signing in with GitHub at https://www.trypreflight.dev/#early-access.

## Machine-readable public content

Public pages support `Accept: text/markdown`. Browser requests continue to receive HTML.

- [Product overview in Markdown](https://www.trypreflight.dev/markdown)
- [Published blog index in Markdown](https://www.trypreflight.dev/markdown/blog)
- [Privacy Policy in Markdown](https://www.trypreflight.dev/markdown/privacy)
- [Terms of Service in Markdown](https://www.trypreflight.dev/markdown/terms)
- [API catalog](https://www.trypreflight.dev/.well-known/api-catalog)
- [Public OpenAPI description](https://www.trypreflight.dev/openapi.json)
- [Authentication instructions](https://www.trypreflight.dev/auth.md)
- [Sitemap](https://www.trypreflight.dev/sitemap.xml)

A published blog post at `/blog/{slug}` is also available at `/markdown/blog/{slug}`.
Only public content is available through these representations. Accounts, projects,
runs, invitations, and admin data are excluded. The API catalog describes actual
read-only content endpoints; it does not advertise external agent execution or payments.
